metadata.scope: Add a force-migration path to apps/api so a physically-deletable tag that still has member_tags references can have those references reassigned to another (destination) tag and then be hard-deleted. New repository functions migrateMemberTagReferences (INSERT OR IGNORE + DELETE to absorb (member_id, dest) PK collisions, returning {sourceReferenceCount,migratedCount}) and forceMigrateAndPhysicalDeleteTagDefinition (validate src/dest existence + dest active + src!=dest, migrate, re-verify countMemberTagReferences(src)===0, then call the existing physicalDeleteTagDefinition). Extend DELETE /admin/tags/:tagId/physical with an optional ?migrateTo=<destTagId> query branch: when absent the issue-1070 409 tag_has_references rejection path is preserved verbatim (AC-7 regression); when present the two-stage migrate->verify->delete flow runs. Add error codes migration_target_not_found(404)/migration_target_inactive(409)/migration_target_same_as_source(400) to ERROR_TO_STATUS, and a new audit action admin.tag.references_migrated (before={tag_id:src,dest,referenceCount}, after={migratedCount,deleted:true}) alongside the existing admin.tag.physically_deleted. No D1 schema migration is required (member_tags has no FK to tag_definitions; the guard and migration are application-level by design). No apps/web change. Force-migration and physical delete are physical-deletion-2-stage: endpoint code + migration SQL + reference guard + audit + tests are implementable in one cycle; only the production runtime mutation is user-gated via runbook. Issue #1117 stays CLOSED. This deliverable includes local implementation, focused tests, and canonical spec sync; commit, push, PR, staging runtime, production mutation, and Issue state changes are user-gated.

metadata.issue_optimization_note: Issue #1117 (= issue-1070 followup-001) was filed against the issue-1070 design boundary (409 tag_has_references rejection). issue-1070 is now landed (countMemberTagReferences / physicalDeleteTagDefinition / 409 tag_has_references exist in current code: tagDefinitions.ts:210-237, tags.ts:59,268-289). This spec is optimized to CURRENT code: (O1) the migration target is a runtime-chosen value, so a fixed DDL migration cannot express it -> dedicated ENDPOINT method confirmed (DELETE /admin/tags/:tagId/physical?migrateTo=<dest>), no new schema migration. (O2) member_tags has NO database FOREIGN KEY to tag_definitions (PRIMARY KEY (member_id, tag_id) only + idx_member_tags_member, migrations/0002_admin_managed.sql:43-51,85-86), so migration/guard are application-level; (member_id, dest) PK collisions are absorbed by INSERT OR IGNORE + DELETE. (O3) the issue-1070 409 rejection path is preserved as the no-migrateTo branch (AC-7 regression). (O4) audit uses appendTagAudit + auditLog.ts (before_json/after_json/actor); AuditAction is RepoBrand<string> so the new admin.tag.references_migrated needs no enum/brand change, and AuditTargetType already includes 'tag'. (O5) migration target validation (not_found/inactive/same-as-source) uses getTagDefinitionByIdRaw + the active column. Latest migration is 0025; no 0026 is added by this task (runtime data op, not DDL). Confirmed unimplemented before this cycle; this cycle implements the dedicated endpoint path locally. Issue stays CLOSED.
